decision_reason: A1 already gives the static unseen classes a physically appropriate ordinal distinction through posture_inclination, and no independent contact-state distinction is supported by the supplied IMUs. The main refinements are therefore directed at the close walkingâjogging relation and the weakly covered frontal elevation of arms. Generic rotational motion is split by body region, while vertical translation and cross-segment motion extent are added to distinguish locomotor dynamics from localized arm motion. Motion regularity is dropped because every supplied A1 prototype has the same level and it provides no split-specific contrast.

attributes.name: motion_intensity
attributes.definition: Overall magnitude and energy of motion within a window, including both linear and rotational components.

attributes.name: cadence
attributes.definition: Rate at which a meaningful periodic motion unit repeats over time. Cadence measures repetitions per unit time, not the total number of repetitions in the recording.

levels.Low: No clear periodic repetition or a slow repetition rate.

attributes.name: smoothness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion changes continuously rather than through sustained rapid fluctuations.

levels.Medium: Moderately smooth motion with some fluctuations.
levels.High: Continuous and smooth motion with little fluctuation.

attributes.name: impulsiveness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion contains short, abrupt, high-magnitude changes or impacts.

levels.Low: Few or no pronounced abrupt peaks.

attributes.name: posture_inclination
attributes.definition: Average gravity-relative inclination of the global load-bearing body configuration within a window, rather than the orientation of an isolated moving limb.

levels.High: Strongly inclined or nearly horizontal relative to gravity.

attributes.name: posture_variability
attributes.definition: Extent to which the global load-bearing body configuration changes relative to gravity within a window, rather than local limb-orientation changes.

attributes.name: upper_limb_rotational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of angular motion of the instrumented right lower arm relative to motion of the trunk and lower limb.

levels.Low: Little or no distinct upper-limb angular motion.
levels.Medium: Moderate upper-limb angular motion or motion largely carried with the body.
levels.High: Prominent upper-limb angular motion relative to the trunk and lower limb.

attributes.name: load_bearing_rotational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of angular motion in the trunk or lower-limb load-bearing configuration during the activity.

levels.Low: Little or no angular motion of the load-bearing configuration.
levels.Medium: Moderate angular motion of the trunk or lower limb.
levels.High: Prominent angular motion of the trunk or lower-limb configuration.

attributes.name: translational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of sustained linear progression or locomotor translation within a window.

levels.High: Prominent sustained translational or locomotor motion.

attributes.name: vertical_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of gravity-aligned translational dynamics, such as repeated body elevation, descent, or vertical propulsion.

levels.Medium: Moderate vertical translation or repeated vertical oscillation.
levels.High: Prominent elevation, descent, or vertical propulsion.

attributes.name: cross_segment_motion_extent
attributes.definition: Extent to which motion is distributed across the instrumented upper limb, trunk, and lower limb rather than concentrated in one body region.

levels.Low: Motion is absent or concentrated mainly in one instrumented body region.
levels.Medium: Motion is appreciable across two instrumented body regions.
levels.High: Motion is broadly distributed across the upper limb, trunk, and lower limb.

operations.reason: Overall motion energy remains an independent ordinal distinction between static activities, walking, and more vigorous locomotor activities.
Repetition rate is physically supported by periodicity and separates static classes and moderate-rate walking from faster cyclic activity.
Sustained rapid signal fluctuation remains distinct from peak impacts and helps transfer between smooth arm or bending motions and less smooth locomotor motions.
Peak abrupt changes provide a supported contrast between controlled arm motion, static postures, and impact-bearing locomotion without duplicating sustained smoothness.

Gravity-relative load-bearing inclination is the direct supported distinction among standing still, sitting and relaxing, and lying down; adding another static-orientation attribute would be redundant.
Global posture change separates isolated arm elevation and static postures from repeated bending of the load-bearing configuration.

Generic rotation conflates arm elevation with waist and knee bending. The forearm, chest, and ankle inventory supports a transferable regional split between isolated upper-limb angular motion and rotation of the load-bearing configuration.
Sustained progression remains the primary distinction between walking and nonlocomotor arm or posture activities and transfers directly from seen locomotor classes.
All supplied A1 class prototypes assign High regularity, so this concept creates no split-specific class contrast and does not improve unseen coverage.

Gravity-aligned translation supplies an independent distinction between level walking and the stronger vertical dynamics represented by climbing stairs, jogging, and jumping, while remaining low for localized arm elevation.
Multisensor motion distribution distinguishes localized frontal arm elevation from whole-body locomotion and load-bearing bends without relying on an unobserved contact state.

semantic_redundancy_review: The retained concepts describe distinct physical factors: total energy, repetition rate, sustained fluctuation, isolated peaks, mean global inclination, variation of global posture, regional angular motion, sustained progression, gravity-aligned translation, and spatial distribution across body segments. Smoothness and impulsiveness are separated as sustained jerk versus short peak events. Translational_motion describes overall progression, whereas vertical_motion describes its gravity-aligned component. The two rotational attributes are region-specific and do not duplicate posture inclination, which concerns mean orientation. Cross_segment_motion_extent measures distribution rather than magnitude or anatomical direction. Motion_regularity was removed because it was constant across all supplied prototypes.

_meta.validation: Semantic schema and complete A1-to-A2 lineage validated; no feature binding performed.
